html:
The May Revolution was a week of events in Buenos Aires in May 1810 that removed the Spanish viceroy and set up a local government, the Primera Junta, on 25 May. It began the independence of Argentina.

News arrived that the French had taken almost all of Spain and the central junta ruling in the king's name had fallen. Creole leaders, backed by the militias of the British invasions, called an open town meeting in Buenos Aires. It voted to remove the viceroy and chose a junta that claimed to rule for the captive king Ferdinand VII.

The junta sent armies to the interior, Paraguay and Upper Peru, with mixed success. Formal independence came at Tucumán in 1816, and the wars were won by San Martín. 25 May is a national holiday in Argentina, and the Plaza de Mayo, where crowds gathered, is the centre of its political life.
sum: The May Revolution was a week of events in Buenos Aires in May 1810 that removed the Spanish viceroy and set up a local government, the Primera Junta, on 25 May. It began the independence of Argentina.
